title: State v. Brown
description: Whether Mr. Brown had a reasonable expectation of privacy during his conversation with his mother in a police interview room, making the surreptitious recording of that conversation a violation of his constitutional rights.
plaintiff_argument: The state argued that Mr. Brown did not possess a reasonable expectation of privacy while at the police station, and therefore, the recording of his conversation with his mother was permissible.
defendant_argument: Mr. Brown argued that the police officers' actions created a reasonable expectation of privacy, and thus the surreptitious recording of his conversation with his mother violated his Fourth Amendment and state constitutional rights.
decision_outcome: The court affirmed the Superior Court's order granting Mr. Brown's motion to suppress the recorded conversation with his mother.

title: Benson v. McKee
description: Whether the Rhode Island General Assembly had the constitutional authority to enact the Reproductive Privacy Act (RPA) and whether the plaintiffs had standing to challenge its enactment.
plaintiff_argument: The plaintiffs argued that the trial justice erred by dismissing their claims for lack of standing, that the General Assembly lacked constitutional authority to enact the RPA, and that their voting rights were suppressed.
defendant_argument: The defendants argued that the plaintiffs lacked standing to bring their claims and that the General Assembly had the constitutional authority to enact the RPA.
decision_outcome: The Supreme Court affirmed the Superior Court's judgment, ruling that the plaintiffs lacked standing to challenge the Reproductive Privacy Act.

title: Zab v. Rhode Island Department of Corrections
description: Whether Rhode Island's civil death statute, which deems life-sentenced prisoners civilly dead and bars them from civil actions, is unconstitutional because it violates their right to access the courts.
plaintiff_argument: The civil death statute is unconstitutional as it violates their fundamental right to access the courts and seek remedies for wrongs, as guaranteed by Article 1, Section 5 of the Rhode Island Constitution.
defendant_argument: The civil death statute is constitutional, does not infringe on the right to access courts, and serves as a legitimate additional sanction for serious criminals, furthering punishment and deterrence.
decision_outcome: The court declared the entirety of Rhode Island's civil death statute (§ 13-6-1) unconstitutional, reversing the lower court's judgments that barred plaintiffs' negligence claims, but affirmed the dismissal of Zab's federal § 1983 claim.

title: Doe v. Brown University
description: Whether the plaintiff's claims under the Rhode Island Civil Rights Act (RICRA) were precluded by prior federal Title IX litigation and whether Article 1, Section 2 of the Rhode Island Constitution creates a private right of action for damages.
plaintiff_argument: The plaintiff argued that her RICRA claims were not dependent on her federal Title IX claims and thus not precluded, and that the Rhode Island Constitution's antidiscrimination clause creates a private right of action against Brown University, which she alleged interfered with her educational contract through its mishandling of her sexual assault.
defendant_argument: The defendants argued that the plaintiff's RICRA claims were barred by issue preclusion due to the prior dismissal of her Title IX claims, and that the Rhode Island Constitution's antidiscrimination clause does not create a private cause of action for damages, nor were they state actors.
decision_outcome: The court affirmed the Superior Court's judgment, dismissing all of the plaintiff's claims under the Rhode Island Civil Rights Act and the Rhode Island Constitution.
